result.title: Counting Beyond Frames: Codec Motion Tells Frozen Diffusion VLMs How Many
result.summary: Counting how many times something happens is among the simplest questions about a video and among the hardest for video-language models, autoregressive and diffusion alike. The difficulty lies between the frames: a model samples only a few of them, while each repetition unfolds as movement in between. Video codecs already record this movement densely as block displacements, and codec-based video models use it to shape their visual input. We are the first to show that this motion provides direct evidence for the count: a candidate count is a testable motion hypothesis, and unwinding the cycles it implies measures how strongly the observed directions support it. We present CoDiCount, a unified training-free framework that turns this test into a count potential and applies it while a frozen diffusion vision-language model (dVLM) denoises its answer. At every denoising step, structured count messages map each option letter, or each grammar-valid edit of an open integer, to the count it expresses and reweight the model's own probabilities within that set. Consistent gains over the official decoders on MotionBench, TOMATO, and SVCBench demonstrate the broad generalization of CoDiCount across diffusion models, datasets, and diverse counting tasks. With CoDiCount, a 7B dVLM outperforms GPT-5.1 and Gemini-2.5-Pro on MotionBench, surpasses GPT-4o and much larger open models on TOMATO, and matches GPT-5.4 on SVCBench.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对视频计数中「帧间运动」难以被稀疏采样捕捉的问题，提出免训练框架 CoDiCount：把候选计数视为可检验的运动假设，用视频编码器的块位移解开周期来度量证据强度，形成计数势，并在冻结扩散 VLM 每个去噪步按该势重加权候选答案概率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「外部视觉证据→候选假设检验→在生成过程中约束答案分布」的流程与 LVR 关注的证据筛选、答案是否真正使用视觉信息、去噪/并行生成中的状态干预有具体联系，可供核查是否可移植到 latent 推理轨迹的验证与贡献分配；但任务限于计数，不是 latent 状态生成研究。
